correctness.rationale: The exact sink cubical model is justified by Ramos Theorem 3.2. The relative pair \((G\times G,D)\) has precisely the \(E\) missing diagonal squares, giving the displayed integral exact sequence. Its map sends graph-cycle tensors to coordinatewise products. Signed rectangle pairs yield individual edge units for both bipartition sizes at least three; yield each saturated equal-row unit for \(2\)-by-\(n\) with \(n\ge3\); and yield a primitive rank-one all-one image for \(2\)-by-\(2\). Hence its cokernel is torsion-free, with the stated integral \(H_1\)/\(H_2\) ranks. The Koszul sign of the label transposition in dimension two and the symmetric/alternating-square identities prove the complete rational eigenspaces. The bundled checker separately reconstructs actual chains for seven sizes, checks \(\partial_1\partial_2=0\), ranks over four primes and 2120 signed character identities. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace the unbounded integral proof.

originality.rationale: A comparison at the level of spaces, parameters, and implications found no published or indexed source that determines the all-size integral homology together with the full side-preserving symmetric-group and particle-swap rational modules for ordered pairs with only vertex coincidences. Chettih--Lütgehetmann treats graphs built from trees with loops and introduces sinks; Ramos gives the general cubical model and explicit tree results, but no evaluated complete-bipartite module theorem. Ramos--Yun concerns configurations with all collisions forbidden: its \(K_{3,3}\) second Betti number is one, whereas the sink variant here has seven. The previously known cycle case \(K_{2,2}\) is explicitly acknowledged as covered; all families with larger sides are not implied by that case. Search failure is not treated as absolute novelty certification.
residual_risks: An unindexed prior treatment may derive the coordinatewise-cycle-product pairing for the same sink configuration family without using that terminology.
The known \(K_{2,2}\) subcase, isomorphic to the four-cycle, was previously computed; novelty is claimed only for the full infinite-family rank-and-equivariant result beyond that boundary.
Additional side-exchange symmetry at equal graph-part sizes is outside the asserted module classification.

value.rationale: The all-size result determines how changing the bipartition from two to at least three vertices changes a natural coordinatewise cycle-product image, including its primitive integer lattice and induced homology. It further resolves the complete side-permutation by particle-swap modules, with Specht \((t-2,2)\) and alternating-square constituents. This addresses the meaningful distinction between permitted vertex collisions and ordinary configurations, and includes an exact infinite-family representation classification rather than a table lookup or a routine isolated case. The \(K_{2,2}\) cycle boundary is acknowledged as prior coverage and is not presented as the discovery.
